summary: Builds an Excel-format invoice from an OrderId, writing it to the path the caller provides. Uses late-bound CreateObject because the customer's deployment doesn't have Excel registered consistently and the harness must tolerate runs where Excel is absent.

inputs.name: orderId
inputs.semantic: Primary key into the Orders table.

inputs.name: targetPath
inputs.semantic: Absolute file path where the .xls workbook is to be saved.

outputs.name: success
outputs.semantic: True iff the workbook was created AND written to targetPath. False on Excel-absent or any I/O failure.

invariants.claim: On the success path the workbook contains exactly one sheet, named 'Invoice', with the order header on rows 1-4 and order lines starting at row 6.
Excel is quit and the COM reference is released before the routine returns — no orphan EXCEL.EXE processes.

com_interop_contracts.contract: Acquires a hidden Excel.Application instance, adds a single workbook, populates cells from DAO data, SaveAs targetPath with format xlExcel8 (.xls), closes, and quits. Visible is explicitly set False so the user never sees the Excel UI.
com_interop_contracts.replacement_hint: ClosedXML 0.105+ for .NET 10. Zero external runtime; produces identical .xlsx output. Excel Interop is unnecessary because the routine doesn't require an active Excel UI.

late_binding_calls.subject: xlApp
late_binding_calls.contract: Dispatches against the Excel.Application instance to create a new empty workbook. Returns a Workbook reference held in xlBook.

late_binding_calls.subject: xlSheet
late_binding_calls.contract: Default-property access on the Worksheet — Cells(row, col).Value reads/writes a single cell. Used in the order-line loop.

on_error_handlers.policy: Err 429 (ActiveX component can't create object) means Excel isn't installed. The handler sets success = False and returns gracefully. Any other error escapes — the routine doesn't try to swallow general failures.
on_error_handlers.translation_hint: C# 10: try { excelApp = CreateExcel(); } catch (COMException ex) when ((uint)ex.HResult == 0x80040154) { return false; }. Or use ClosedXML and skip the try entirely.

side_effects.description: Writes a .xls workbook to targetPath via SaveAs.
Spawns and terminates an EXCEL.EXE process; visible only via Task Manager during the run.

edge_cases.description: Excel is not installed on the host. CreateObject('Excel.Application') raises Err 429; the handler returns False without producing a file.
edge_cases.behavior: Return False; no file written; no Excel process spawned.

edge_cases.description: targetPath is a read-only location. SaveAs raises Err 1004 (Method 'SaveAs' of object failed). The On Error Goto branch returns False without leaving an EXCEL.EXE process — the Quit call is in the cleanup section that always runs.
edge_cases.behavior: Return False; no file written; Excel quit cleanly.

open_questions.question: Should the .NET 10 port keep .xls output for backward compatibility, or switch to .xlsx (Open XML)? ClosedXML supports both but defaults to .xlsx.
